title: TanStack Start application surface registry
description: The enumerated declaration `scripts/template/start-contract.ts` validates. A server-rendered application is the rare surface whose defects are silent: a `types` entry that does not resolve fails the typechecker and never fails the build, because esbuild ignores `types` entirely; a build-time variable missing from a deploy job's environment compiles to the literal `undefined` and every truthiness-guarded consumer just stops rendering; and a route whose asset prefix disagrees with the served directory returns 404 for rewritten URLs in the built Worker alone. So the surface is declared here — the shared TypeScript base, the server-render response policy, the worker configuration, the built-artifact shape, the router options, the asset namespace and the per-application route tree — and reconciled against the tree. `mode` is the load-bearing field: `skeleton` asserts, positively, that no application of this stack exists anywhere in the tracked tree; `active` asserts every declared artefact exists and runs every rule over it.

mode.description: The declared tree state. It is compared with the derived state before any other rule runs, and a disagreement in either direction is the first error.

tsconfigPath.description: The shared TypeScript base every application of this stack extends. In every mode it must exist, be an ordinary in-tree file with exactly one hard link, and extend the repository base — a base that restates a weaker option set while calling itself strict is the defect this registry exists to make visible.

devServer.description: The runtime a developer actually runs this stack under. It is declared rather than assumed because the two answers differ in kind: the built worker under the pinned Cloudflare CLI exercises the production artefact, while a bundler dev server resolves modules at request time and fails server renders with `Cannot find module` on internal subpath imports that the build bundles. The second answer is a refusal a reasoned waiver may lift.

viteDevWaiver.description: The reasoned waiver that lifts the development-server refusal, or null. A waiver keeps the finding a decision rather than an obstacle: the guard prints the reason it was given, so the next reader inherits the argument instead of rediscovering the defect.

proxyRegistryPath.description: The development proxy route registry this surface reconciles against. It belongs to a declared capability dependency rather than to this capability, so it is READ as data with a named notice when it is absent and never imported — a generation-time dependency guarantee expires at generation, and a static import would turn a diagnostic into a module-load crash in a tree a downstream project is free to create.

types.description: The `compilerOptions.types` entries the shared base declares. Empty is the correct answer for this stack: modern routers register route types through declaration merging rather than through an ambient global type library, and a worker environment is modelled structurally in an ambient declaration file the application owns.

forbiddenTypes.description: Type entries that must never appear, whether or not they resolve. The reserved entry is the one this stack shipped with: it named a subpath the router package does not export, so the typechecker failed with TS2688 while the build stayed green, because esbuild ignores `types`.

ssr.description: The server-render response policy, declared as a matrix rather than discovered from a handler.

mode.description: Buffered or streaming. Buffered is the declared default because streaming backpressure and abort behaviour on this worker runtime is unproven, which is a statement about a date rather than a law — so streaming is a refusal a reasoned waiver may lift.

methods.description: The methods a document route serves. Exactly GET and HEAD: a document is a read, and HEAD is answered with GET semantics minus the body.

methodRejection.description: What any other method receives. A 405 naming the methods it would have accepted, because a document route that answers 404 to a POST has told the caller the wrong thing.

cacheControl.description: The cache directive every response class carries — 200, 302, 4xx and 5xx alike. These payloads are per-user and must never be shared-cached, and a directive applied to the success path alone is the version of this rule that leaks.

determinism.description: The fixed timezone and locale the server render and the first client render share. A locale or timezone drift between the two is a classic hydration-mismatch source, and it presents as an unrelated flake rather than as an error.

worker.description: The source worker configuration every declared application writes by hand.

compatibilityDate.description: One fleet-consistent date rather than whichever default the scaffolding emitted, so two workers in one repository cannot disagree about runtime semantics.

compatibilityFlags.description: Must contain the Node compatibility flag: the server bundle of this stack requires it, and without it the worker fails at module evaluation rather than at a request.

workersDev.description: Pinned false. A workers.dev subdomain is a second public origin nobody enumerated.

previewUrls.description: Pinned false, for the same reason.

serviceBindings.description: The closed allowlist of service bindings. A binding absent from this list is refused rather than warned about: the whole safety argument of a narrow binding set is that a leak between two services is structurally impossible, and one undeclared binding dissolves it.

forbiddenBindingKinds.description: Binding families that must be absent or empty in both the source configuration and the built artefact.

harnessOnlyVariables.description: Variables a test harness injects that must never reach a deploy artefact. A harness oracle shipped to production is a hard failure and not a warning.

build.description: The build outputs and the contract over the generated worker configuration. These are the artefacts a deploy ships, and the only proof of a build that is portable to a template with no application.

serverModule.description: The entry module name inside the generated server directory, as the generated worker configuration spells it.

assetsDirectory.description: The asset directory the generated worker configuration declares, relative to itself.

assetsPrefix.description: The emitted asset directory every application shares. Rewriting document URLs to a different prefix does not move the physical directory the asset binding serves, which made every rewritten URL 404 in the built worker while the development server stayed green.

buildTimeVariables.description: Variables the bundler INLINES at build time. If a deploy job omits one from the build step's environment the expression compiles to the literal `undefined`, the bundle ships, the worker boots, nothing throws, and every truthiness-guarded consumer silently stops rendering. There is no runtime signal anywhere.

router.description: The router options that are decisions rather than defaults.

defaultPreload.description: Router-wide speculation, pinned false. Only source-audited high-frequency link sites should preload on intent.

defaultErrorComponent.description: Whether every route carries an error boundary. Without one the router installs NO catch boundary for a match, so a render throw escapes to the nearest ancestor gate and is misreported as a session failure — or, on a public route, hits nothing at all.

apps.description: Every application of this stack. Empty is the declared answer for a template that generates none, and `mode` is what makes that assertion rather than silence.

app.description: One application of this stack. Every path field except `directory` is relative to `directory`, so an application can be moved without rewriting its own declaration.

directory.description: The application directory. The naming rule is enforced rather than suggested, because a directory that does not match is a directory the deploy-coverage oracle cannot map to a job — and renaming a job away from its directory is a violation rather than a silent skip.

basePath.description: The public prefix the bundler serves this application under, always with a trailing slash.

routerBasepath.description: The router basepath, which is the public prefix without its trailing slash. Declared separately because the two are spelled differently in two files and drift between them is invisible until a route 404s in the built worker.

assetsDir.description: The emitted asset directory, which must equal the shared prefix.

routeTree.description: The generated route tree. It is governed as a COMMITTED artefact rather than a regenerable one: tracked, absent from the ignore list, and excluded from the formatter and the linter, because the generator emits casts and unorganized imports in its raw style and a freshly built tree fails a lint pass that a checked-in copy does not.

ambientDeclarations.description: The ambient declaration files this application owns. They are what replaces a global type library: the worker environment is modelled structurally so the application never needs a platform types package in its empty `types` list.

clientOnlyModules.description: Modules that must not enter the server bundle. A server graph and a client graph are different graphs and the difference is declared rather than discovered: a dependency that does not build on the worker runtime enters through a dynamic import the server build eliminates.

proxyRouteId.description: The route id in the development proxy registry that fronts this application, or null. Declared by id and reconciled only when that registry is present.
